ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #19
====

GRADE: Grade 1
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. Many unrelated topics with no link
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

2. When practising Word Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Word Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Word Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Word Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.

3. When practising Phonics, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Phonics.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonics.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Phonics.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Phonics.

4. When practising Pre Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Pre Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Pre Reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Pre Reading.

5. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. goed
   C. went
   D. goes

6. When practising Pre-Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Pre-Writing.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Pre-Writing.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Pre-Writing.

7. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only a describing word
   C. Only an action
   D. Only a joining word

8. When practising Connected text and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text and fluency.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Connected text and fluency.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Connected text and fluency.

9. When practising Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Comprehension.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Comprehension.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Comprehension.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.

10. When practising Language Welcome and, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Language Welcome and.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Language Welcome and.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Language Welcome and.

11. When practising Attentive listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Attentive listening.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Attentive listening.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive listening.

12. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Language School and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Pre Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Phonics and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Word Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

2. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.

8. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Word Reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
